web_evidence.title: The Book of Lost Friends — Penguin Random House Library Marketing
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s authorized prologue excerpt sustains third-person narration centered on an unnamed teacher, establishing a third-person frame section.

web_evidence.title: The Book of Lost Friends: A Novel — Everand ebook preview
web_evidence.note: The licensed sustained preview labels Chapter 1 as Hannie Gossett and Chapter 2 as Benedetta Silva; both chapters narrate their story scenes extensively in first person.

web_evidence.title: Lisa Wingate Writing Styles in The Book of Lost Friends
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view analysis explicitly identifies the prologue’s third-person narrator, the bulk novel’s two first-person narrators, and Benny’s first-person epilogue.

web_evidence.title: Book Review: The Book of Lost Friends — Colloquium
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes the main structure as alternating first-person narratives from Hannie and Benny, corroborating that the two timelines do not alternate grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: The Book of Lost Friends — Historical Novel Society
web_evidence.note: This reputable review confirms alternating chapters between Hannie’s and Benny’s narratives and quotes Benny addressing the reader from her narrating position.

search_log: Searched “The Book of Lost Friends Lisa Wingate excerpt first chapter” and opened sustained Bookreporter and Everand previews.
Searched “The Book of Lost Friends first person narrator” and “point of view dual timeline”; results consistently identified Hannie and Benny as the two principal narrative strands.
Searched the author and publisher domains for an authorized excerpt; Penguin Random House supplied the third-person prologue but no explicit whole-book POV statement.
Searched “The Book of Lost Friends first-person Hannie Benny” and found an explicit whole-book description of alternating first-person narratives in Colloquium.
Searched specifically for the prologue and epilogue narration; BookRags identified the prologue as third person, the bulk as two first-person narrators, and the epilogue as Benny’s first person.
Goodreads pages, generic summaries, retailer snippets, and audiobook-narrator references were inspected for discovery but not relied on as structural evidence.
person_note: The book's base narration is FIRST: its two sustained timelines are narrated by participating first-person narrators, Hannie in 1875 and Benny in 1987, and the epilogue also returns to Benny's first-person voice. Goodreads passages expose both main voices, and a licensed preview independently confirms their sustained first-person chapters. A brief third-person prologue is genuine narration but is not a co-controlling base strand, so it does not override the person of the rest of the novel.
